about.title: Why the name Niyosh
about.body1: Niyosh is maintained by Soheil Onsori, a law graduate (LL.B.) and developer building privacy-first AI tools for legal work. He is the author of two prior tools: Karnam (post-meeting legal analysis) and Namag (contract clause analysis). He holds a Legal Engineering Certification from Harvey Academy and Anthropic's AI Fluency credential. His focus is the intersection of legal reasoning, applied AI, and compliance — GDPR, the EU AI Act, and § 201 StGB. The builder is not a licensed attorney: all outputs are designed for review by qualified legal professionals.
about.body2: Niyosh — from the Middle Persian niyōš: to listen, to hear. The word lives on in Persian today as niyōšā — one who listens with attention and care. I named this tool after that idea: a companion that listens to the meeting so the lawyer can focus on the conversation.

responsibility.title: User responsibility
responsibility.text: The user is responsible for verifying local recording laws before using audio capture. If recording is restricted or prohibited in the meeting's jurisdiction, the user must disable audio capture before the meeting starts. This responsibility lies with the user, not the builder.
